title: Harry Walker taught Lovett drums and reading in Alexandria
summary: His only teacher was a saxophonist-bandleader named Harry Walker, who taught him to read and led a ragtime band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: We would like to start, Baby, by asking a question of the type of training you had in playing drums, the education? Where did you learn to play drums, Baby?
In Alexandria, Louisiana.
From whom?
A fellow by the name of Harry Walker.
He was a drummer?
No, no, he was a saxophone man.
Well, how was he able to teach you to play the drums?

Well, he was an older fellow than I, you know, and he was about through then, ready to quit the business and he lived one block from me and I had to go around -- he had me to come round to his house about twice a week when I was a kid.
He probably taught you how to keep the
Oh sure.
Well you can learn drums from other musicians. I learned some drumming from Ben Canard, believe it or not. I really have. The great tenor sax player.
Yeah. They know too. So Harry taught me everything I knew, how to read and everything else.
Well, that's great, that's great, and that was about -- did you study with anyone else, drums, or music?
No.
That was it?
That was it, yeah.
He taught you how to read as a young boy down in Alexandria, Louisiana?
Yeah.
And you really developed from there.
I was wearing short pants then.
Yeah, I can believe it. He must have been a wonderful man.
Oh he was.
He was a band leader?
Oh yes.
What did you say his instrument was?
Saxophone and clarinet.
What kind of music was his band playing in those days?
Just strictly reading.
No but I mean -- well what was it, military marches?
Well we called it Ragtime.
Ragtime?
Yeah, back in those days.
